historical_reconstructions.title: Apollo 1
historical_reconstructions.summary: A cabin fire during a ground rehearsal propagated rapidly through a pressurized pure-oxygen atmosphere. Three astronauts died.

historical_reconstructions.title: Apollo 13
historical_reconstructions.summary: Ground heaters powered at 65 V damaged thermostat contacts designed for 28 V. Prolonged heating damaged oxygen-tank wire insulation before flight; later electrical operation initiated the tank failure.

knowledge_card_annotations.notes: Diffusion-dominated spherical flames are a useful still-microgravity limit, not a universal shape or color under forced ventilation. Exact card source points to the general PSI portal.
Supplied 13.6% and 18% limits refer to different flow/orientation configurations; they should not be treated as a universal paired material limit. Primary PSI catalogue source remains linked.
NASA FLEX/CFI research supports low-temperature combustion after hot-flame extinction; the full stated temperature ranges and vapor-cloud sequence require run-specific verification.
NASA SAME-R description confirms particle-size/moment diagnostics and near-IR size sensitivity. Exact 55%/66.7% test miss rates remain supplied report claims, not universal detector probabilities.

NASA Expedition 11 press kit describes DAFT instruments arriving in 2004 as a risk-mitigation experiment in support of SAME. This chronology does not support a literal assertion that DAFT reused returned SAME hardware; dust/smoke discrimination is supported.
NTRS 20240005151 confirms exploration-atmosphere test presentation metadata; mission values remain research/test references and are not guaranteed operational mission requirements.

Arithmetic partial pressures match the stated total-pressure/oxygen pairs. At the app EVA preset 85% and 29.6 kPa, pO2 is3.65 psia; 4.30 psia describes 100% O2 at4.3 psia. NASA NTRS 20160001047 notes concentration matters beyond equal oxygen partial pressure.

NASA 2024 FM2 poster describes planned lunar-surface hardware and short-duration centrifuge/parabolic evidence, not completed long-duration lunar-surface telemetry. Current completeness of all PSI holdings has not been independently established.

NASA 2024 Saffire VI presentation and2025 vehicle-model event table support the cited material/atmosphere matrix and Nomex non-ignition. Conditions vary across events; not every point shares one universal flow history.
NASA NTRS 20240015307 poster describes21% O2/14.7 psia and34% O2/8.2 psia test atmospheres, lunar centrifuge evidence and planned lunar hardware. It does not establish completed lunar-surface tests.

NASA NTRS 20260003925 (May 2026) abstract explicitly identifies material flammability as the critical 8.2 psia/34–40%O2 hurdle and 70% of the assessed subsystems needing material replacements. This is the assessed ECLSS set, not70% of all spacecraft hardware.

NASA NTRS API 20260001600 returns curated conference paper Spacecraft Fire Safety Predictions using Verified Saffire Model, ICES-2026-092, July 2026. Its abstract describes FDS validation against Saffire remote sensors and subsequent hazard scenarios. This does not validate PyroZero surrogate equations.

NASA Spinoff 2020 confirms nine ISS fine-water-mist extinguishers replaced original CO2 devices. A blanket statement that ISS Halon units were replaced or that FLEX alone caused adoption is not established by that source.

AIAA Aerospace America reports the crew debrief directly and confirms a second-to-last-day smoke alarm around 80,000 miles from home. The alarm cause remains unconfirmed; bump/camera/lunar-dust explanations must not be presented as established causes.
NASA incident sources confirm the three events and safety mechanisms. Apollo13 tank conditions must not be interpreted as cabin atmosphere, and Mir accounts disagree about fire duration.
NASA reduced-gravity combustion guide supports the CIR/MSG/Cygnus hardware families. Shared or related equipment does not prove identical experiment configurations or response envelopes.

AWS Open Data registry confirms public nasa-psi S3resource, but its listed resource description names DSI/OASIS data. It does not prove a complete PSI combustion-catalogue mirror. PSI portal and AWS entry are valid distinct access routes.

Habitat-only coverage is a PyroZero product scope rule. The absolute statement that rocket propellant combustion is independent of gravity is not established by a general PSI portal link; high injection inertia can reduce buoyancy relevance without making gravity universally irrelevant.
